content.value_statement: AI image generators often change character details between images. This skill gives structured prompts, reference sheet patterns, and LoRA guidance for consistent results.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to build turnaround sheets with front, side, back, and three-quarter views.
Provides prompt patterns for expression sheets with consistent facial traits.
Shows how to document character colors, outfit details, proportions, and style keywords.
Describes a reusable description anchor technique for stable character prompts.
Gives LoRA usage guidance for projects that need many consistent images.
Includes common consistency failures and practical mitigation steps.
limitations: Requires access to the belt CLI and supported inference.sh image applications for command examples.
Does not train a LoRA model by itself or prepare training datasets automatically.
Cannot guarantee perfect identity consistency across every image model or seed.
Examples are prompt guidance and may need adjustment for specific art styles.

use_cases.title: Build a Game Character Reference
use_cases.description: Create consistent front, side, back, expression, and outfit references for a playable character.

use_cases.title: Keep Comic Characters Stable
use_cases.description: Use detailed description anchors and color notes to preserve character identity across panels.

use_cases.title: Prepare a LoRA Character Brief
use_cases.description: Organize visual traits, trigger words, scale guidance, and reference requirements before training.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Character Sheet
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one character concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a simple character design sheet for a new character. Include a detailed visual description, colors, outfit notes, and a front-view image prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Create Turnaround Prompts
prompt_templates.scenario: Generate consistent prompts for multiple views.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this character description into front, three-quarter, side, and back-view prompts. Keep all identity details consistent and only change the viewing angle.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Expression Sheet
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan face references for acting and animation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create six expression prompts for this character: neutral, happy, angry, sad, surprised, and thinking. Preserve hair, eye color, face structure, and style.

prompt_templates.title: Design a LoRA Consistency Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a long-running project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my character bible for LoRA readiness. Identify missing visual details, propose trigger words, recommend scale ranges, and list prompts for validation images.

output_examples.input: A fantasy courier needs a repeatable concept art reference.
output_examples.output: A full design sheet plan with a 50-word anchor, color palette, turnaround prompts, outfit variants, and expression prompts.

output_examples.input: A visual novel team needs the same protagonist in many scenes.
output_examples.output: A character bible structure with stable traits, default pose notes, emotion prompts, and LoRA usage recommendations.

output_examples.input: An artist has inconsistent hair and eye colors across generations.
output_examples.output: A mitigation checklist using exact color names, hex values, repeated prompt structure, and early placement of key identity details.

best_practices: Write one detailed description anchor and reuse it exactly across related prompts.
Document exact colors, proportions, clothing, accessories, and distinguishing marks before generating variants.
Use LoRA or image-to-image workflows when a project needs many consistent images.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on vague labels like young, cool, or stylish for identity-critical traits.
Do not change prompt structure heavily between views when character consistency matters.
Do not skip expression and turnaround references for characters used in ongoing projects.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create character reference sheets for AI image workflows, including views, expressions, colors, outfits, and consistency notes.

faq.question: Does it generate images directly?
faq.answer: It provides belt CLI examples for image generation, but image output depends on your installed tools and service access.

faq.question: Can it make one character look identical every time?
faq.answer: It improves consistency with repeatable prompts and references, but exact identity depends on the model, seed, and workflow.

faq.question: When should I use LoRA?
faq.answer: Use LoRA when a project needs many images of the same character across poses, scenes, or outfits.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill workflows.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare the character role, age range, visual style, key colors, outfit details, and any required poses or expressions.
